sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Lehigh County, PA?
sections.html:
Deeds for Lehigh County property are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds Division in Room 122 of the Lehigh County Courthouse at 455 W. Hamilton Street, Allentown, PA 18101. The phone number is 610-782-3162, and the office is open Monday through Friday, 8:00 until 4:30. Parcel identification, called GIS PIN certification, ends earlier, at 3:45 in the afternoon, so bring a deed that needs a new PIN in the morning or early afternoon.

The office closes on major holidays and on any day the President Judge of the Court of Common Pleas directs. For a seller the practical job is simple: whoever handles your closing, whether a title company or an attorney, files the deed and the payoff paperwork. You still want to know the fees, because they show up on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What are the Lehigh County deed recording fees?
sections.html:
A deed of any type costs $81.25 to record under the fee schedule effective January 1, 2026. The fee covers up to four pages, four names and one PIN certification. Anything beyond those limits is billed separately.

Lehigh County recording fees, effective January 1, 2026 (source: Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds fee schedule)
DocumentFee
Deed, all types$81.25
Mortgage$81.25
Satisfaction piece$71.75
Release of mortgage$71.75
Assignment of mortgage$71.75
Deed of dedication$69.75
Easement or right-of-way$69.75
Quiet title action$28.50
Power of attorney$18.50

Extras are small but add up on a complicated parcel:

  • Each page over four costs $2.00, and each name over four costs $0.50.
  • Each additional PIN costs $10.00, so a deed that covers several parcels costs more.
  • Each electronic notation costs $2.00.
  • A rejected document costs $10.00 each time, and a returned check costs $20.00.
  • Mailing documents back costs $3.00 each unless you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

An overpayment of $10.00 or less is forfeited, and the office does not refund fees for a document sent twice by mistake. Double-check the amount before you send it.

sections.h2: Can I record a Lehigh County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The office accepts electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Because those platforms calculate fees and taxes as you submit, fewer documents are rejected, and the county says documents are usually recorded the same day. A rejected filing can be corrected and sent back right away.

Maps and plans, including subdivision plats, can be electronically recorded through the same three vendors. The division does not keep a paper copy of a map that was recorded electronically.

Certified copies are not sold online. They must be made at the Recorder of Deeds office, at a cost of $1.50 more per document than a plain copy. Plain copies are $0.50 per page in person and $1.00 per page by mail.

sections.h2: How are old Lehigh County deeds searched?
sections.html:
The division holds records back to 1812, the year Lehigh County was formed from part of Northampton County. All of it is public except military discharge papers (DD-214), which the office records for free and keeps private. Staff are not authorized to do your search or research for you, so you search yourself.

  • LANDEX Webstore: free searching, with a fee to view or print a document, aimed at occasional users.
  • LANDEX Remote: a pay-as-you-go service at $0.15 a minute and $0.10 for each page loaded, built for heavy users, with an Index Book tab covering 1812 to 1983.
  • Lehigh County Online Records Access: requires an account and a yearly fee arranged through the county Fiscal Office.
  • In person: the public review area on the first floor of the courthouse, open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning until 4:00 in the afternoon

If you inherited a house and the paper trail is thin, the index books may turn up an old deed or an unreleased mortgage before a buyer's title search does.

sections.h2: What transfer tax is due when a Lehigh County house sells?
sections.html:
Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent realty transfer tax on the value of the property, and the Recorder of Deeds collects it with the recording fee. According to the state Department of Revenue, the seller and the buyer are jointly and severally liable. School districts and municipalities may add a local share, and the rate differs by location, so ask the Recorder of Deeds or your closing agent for the total on your parcel, especially if the house is inside a city.

Exemptions exist for some family transfers, transfers by will or intestate succession, and transfers to government bodies. If you claim one, the state's REV-183 Statement of Value is the document that records the reason.

sections.h2: What else can end up on the Lehigh County record for a house?
sections.html:
A sale is not the only event that touches a parcel. Farmland owners record Act 319 preferential assessment filings at $33.00 with no extra charge for added pages or names, and covenant filings under Act 515 carry the same $33.00. An Agricultural Security Area ordinance costs $28.50. Easements and rights-of-way cost $69.75. A lease over 30 years costs $59.75. Financing statements under the Uniform Commercial Code cost $110.00 flat.

Release paperwork matters for sellers more than most. When a loan is paid off at closing, the lender files a satisfaction piece ($71.75) or release of mortgage ($71.75), and the mortgage stays on the record until that happens. If you are selling a house you inherited, look for old mortgages that were paid decades ago but never released, because a buyer's title company will flag them. A notary commission and bond cost $33.50 in the same office.

Plans and maps follow a different scale. A subdivision, survey or stormwater plan costs $35.00 for the first page and $25.00 for each added page, and a condominium plan costs $40.00 and $25.00. Highway, mining and railroad maps cost $15.00 and $3.00. These matter if you are splitting a lot before you sell.

sections.h2: What is Lehigh County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Lehigh County covers 348 square miles in the Lehigh Valley, about 64 miles northwest of Philadelphia and 93 miles west of New York City. It was formed on March 6, 1812, and Allentown is the county seat. The 2020 census counted 374,557 people in the county, and Allentown alone had 125,845. The 2025 estimate is 384,383.

Blue Mountain forms the northern edge of the county and South Mountain the southern edge, with the Lehigh River draining most of the land between them. Winters are cold and summers are hot and humid; Allentown averages roughly 32 inches of snow a year, which is worth knowing when a buyer looks at the roof, gutters and heating system.

  • Cities and boroughs: Allentown, Bethlehem (mostly in Northampton County), Emmaus, Catasauqua, Fountain Hill, Slatington, Coplay, Macungie, Coopersburg and Alburtis.
  • Colleges: Cedar Crest, Muhlenberg, DeSales University, Penn State Lehigh Valley and Lehigh Carbon Community College.
  • Travel: Lehigh Valley International Airport sits in Hanover Township, LANta runs the local buses, and I-78 and PA 309 meet in the county.

The oldest continuously occupied building in the county is Shelter House in Emmaus, built in 1734, and the county contains housing from every era since. Older homes can bring title questions, such as old easements or a lien that was never released, which the recording office's records can help answer.

faqs.q: What is the Lehigh County recording fee for a deed?
faqs.a: A deed costs $81.25 under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. That covers four pages, four names and one PIN certification, with extra pages at $2.00 and extra names at $0.50.

faqs.q: Where is the Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is in Room 122 of the courthouse at 455 W. Hamilton Street in Allentown. It is open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the number is 610-782-3162.

faqs.q: Can I get a certified copy of a Lehigh County deed online?
faqs.a: No. Certified copies are not available online and must be made at the office, at $1.50 more per document than a regular copy. Regular copies cost $0.50 per page in person.

faqs.q: How far back do Lehigh County records go?
faqs.a: The records start in 1812, when the county was formed. LANDEX covers index, deed, mortgage, map and miscellaneous records from 1812 to the present.

faqs.q: Are Lehigh County deeds recorded the same day?
faqs.a: Electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC or ePN are usually recorded the same day. Paper filings depend on the queue, and a rejected paper filing costs $10.00.
